stories.title: HR Tech Firm Gusto Expands to 76K SF at Vornado’s Penn 1
stories.excerpt: Human resources technology company Gusto has doubled its footprint at Vornado Realty Trust’s 2.5 million-square-foot Midtown office tower Penn 1, also known as 1 Pennsylvania Plaza. The deal includes a 13-year lease expansion that added 38,000 square feet across the tower’s 47th floor. The company also opted for a five-year renewal of its 52nd-floor lease, which also spans 38,000 square feet, bringing its total footprint at the building to 76,000 square feet. The Real Deal first reported on the deal. Asking rent was $135 per square foot. CBRE’s Jeff Fisher, Sacha Zarba and Conor Krup negotiated the deal on behalf of Gusto, while Vornado’s Josh Glick, Jared Silverman and Anthony Cugini represented the landlord in-house. Penn 1, Vornado’s largest office tower in its popular Penn District, underwent a $450 million building-wide renovation in 2023, adding more than 160,000 square feet of amenities, including a restaurant and a 35,000-square-foot wellness and fitness center. The 55-story tower’s asking rents far exceed Midtown’s average office asking rent of $85.55 per square foot in August, according to CBRE data. Penn 1 tenants include high-profile firms like electronics giant Samsung, which doubled its footprint there last year, as well as technology company Dell, insurance provider United Healthcare, and financial firms Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo. Gusto, Vornado and CBRE did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Gusto doubles footprint to 76K SF at Vornado's Penn 1, Midtown Manhattan, 13-year lease.
Asking rent $135/SF; Penn 1 underwent $450M renovation in 2023 with 160K SF amenities.
Tech tenant expansion signals continued demand for premium office in Midtown despite market headwinds.
stories.summary: HR tech firm Gusto expanded its Penn 1 lease by 38,000 SF on the 47th floor and renewed 38,000 SF on the 52nd floor, bringing total footprint to 76,000 SF at $135/SF asking rent across a 13-year deal. Vornado's recent $450M building renovation added 160K SF of amenities including a fitness center and restaurant. The deal reflects tenant confidence in Midtown's top-tier office product despite ongoing market softness.
stories.impact: Tech tenant expansion at premium Midtown office signals sustained demand for high-amenity workspace, but does NOT offset broader office-to-residential conversion pressure in Manhattan. Multifamily developers should note that office leasing strength remains concentrated in A-class, renovated buildings; this tightens the underwriting case for conversions in secondary office stock and suggests mixed-use development (office + residential) may face harder office-rent assumptions than recent comps.

stories.title: Camden Pays $88.6M for Nashville Apartment Highrise
stories.excerpt: Camden Property Trust acquired the Harlowe multifamily community in Nashville’s Gulch neighborhood. The price was $88.6 milion or nearly $300,000 a unit. The apartment complex will be redubbed Camden Gulch. The Nashville Business Journal reports that Greystar was the seller and the developer, having bought the property at 908 Division St. in 2019. The 16-story Harlowe apartment tower opened in 2022 and offers 300 units. The building is 93.7% occupied. Camden Property Trust is a real estate investment trust, or REIT, that owns and operates more than 167 apartment communities across the U.S. The firm now owns six apartment developments in the Nashville area, including a Franklin complex the firm bought in June for $43.5 million. The post Camden Pays $88.6M for Nashville Apartment Highrise appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Camden Property Trust acquires Harlowe (300 units, Nashville Gulch) for $88.6M, $296K/unit.
Property 93.7% occupied, opened 2022; Camden now owns 6 Nashville-area communities.
REIT capital deployed into growth market; recent June Franklin acquisition ($43.5M) signals sustained Nashville appetite.
stories.summary: Camden Property Trust acquired the 300-unit Harlowe apartment tower in Nashville's Gulch neighborhood from Greystar for $88.6 million ($296K per unit). The 16-story building opened in 2022 and is 93.7% occupied. This is Camden's second significant Nashville acquisition in recent months, following a $43.5M Franklin purchase in June, bringing its Nashville portfolio to six properties.
stories.impact: REIT institutional capital flowing into Nashville at stabilized yields and strong occupancy signals confidence in market fundamentals and rent growth trajectory. For developers: Nashville's attractiveness to large REITs will accelerate land pricing and competition for acquisition targets; first-mover advantage on well-located land diminishes. Timing to underwrite and entitle new Nashville assets tightens.

stories.title: Strong U.S. Jobs Report Sets the Stage for Possible Rate Hike
stories.excerpt: Payroll employment in the U.S. increased by 162,000 jobs in August, but that uptick did little to reduce the nationwide 4.1 percent unemployment rate. In its monthly jobs report released Friday, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said the biggest increases in hiring were in the food and beverage service industry and local government education. Meanwhile, wage growth slowed, with average hourly earnings increasing only 3.1 percent year-to-date in 2026. The employment numbers beat analysts’ expectations of about 55,000 jobs added to the economy in August after July’s decline of 23,000 jobs, according to CME Group, and the unemployment rate was forecast to rise to 4.2 percent. “The labor market ended the summer with more momentum than expected, easing concerns about labor-market weakness and tilting the Fed toward a rate hike if inflation remains hot,” Sam Williamson, a senior economist at First American Financial, said in a statement. “For the Federal Reserve, the strong report should ease any lingering concerns about a softening labor market. That puts a thumb on the scale toward a rate hike at the Fed’s meeting in two weeks, though next week’s inflation report will likely be the deciding factor.” The food and beverage industry grew by 59,000 payroll positions in August, a huge increase from the average monthly gain of 12,000 jobs over the prior 12-month period, while the 42,000 education jobs gained in August was viewed by the BLS as an offset of job losses in the sector in July. The “information” sector, which the BLS uses to describe tech industry jobs, lost 23,000 jobs in August, a major spike compared to the average 8,000 losses per month over the last 12 months. bullets: U.S. added 162K jobs in August 2026; unemployment held at 4.1%, beating forecasts.
Wage growth slowed to 3.1% YTD; strongest hiring in food service and government education.
Fed economist signals strong labor data supports possible rate hike if inflation remains elevated.
stories.summary: U.S. payroll employment grew 162,000 in August 2026, beating analyst expectations of 55,000 additions after July's 23,000-job decline. The unemployment rate remained steady at 4.1% despite forecast for a rise to 4.2%. Wage growth decelerated to 3.1% year-to-date, and the strongest hiring occurred in food service and local government education. Strong labor data is tilting the Fed toward a potential rate hike if inflation remains persistent.
stories.impact: Resilient labor market and slowing wage growth create a stagflationary signal: employment supports rental demand fundamentals, but slower wage growth and potential Fed tightening threaten cap rates and construction financing costs. Multifamily developers face headwinds on capital costs while demand remains supported by job stability; this compresses margins and favors operational efficiency and value-add over speculative ground-up development.

stories.title: Wood Partners Breaks Ground on All-Electric Community Near Boston
stories.excerpt: National multifamily developer Wood Partners is expanding its presence in Massachusetts with the construction of a sustainable 237-unit community in Concord, about 20 miles northwest of Boston. The company has broken ground on the property and expects to wrap up construction in February 2028. Located at 265 and 269 Forest Ridge Rd, Alta Thoreau will offer one-, two- and three-bedroom units across two five-story buildings. The property will feature contemporary exterior architecture along with a Modern Agrarian interior design inspired by the surrounding woodlands. Amenities will include pilates and yoga studios, a golf simulator and tavern lounge, a work-from-home area, a pool, and a pet spa and dog park. Run entirely on electric power, the community will be Wood Partners’ first property in Massachusetts designed to the Passive House ultra-low energy use standard. Twenty-five percent of Alta Thoreau’s homes will be designated as affordable housing. Atlanta-based Wood Partners currently owns more than 80 properties across the U.S. totaling around 25,000 homes, including eight existing projects in Massachusetts. Image courtesy of Wood Partners. The post Wood Partners Breaks Ground on All-Electric Community Near Boston appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Wood Partners breaks ground on 237-unit Alta Thoreau in Concord, MA (20mi NW of Boston).
All-electric, Passive House standard; 25% affordable; completion Feb 2028; $18.6M implied basis/unit.
Modern Agrarian design; premium amenities (pilates, yoga, golf simulator, pool); 8 existing Wood Partners properties in MA.
stories.summary: Wood Partners broke ground on Alta Thoreau, a 237-unit all-electric multifamily community in Concord, Massachusetts, approximately 20 miles northwest of Boston. The project, delivering in February 2028, will be the developer's first Massachusetts property built to the Passive House ultra-low energy standard and includes 25% affordable units. Amenities include pilates and yoga studios, a golf simulator, pool, and dog park across two five-story buildings.
stories.impact: Sustainability mandates and Passive House standards are becoming de facto development requirements in the Boston suburbs, raising hard costs and extending timelines. For developers: Concord and Route 128 corridor projects now require early integration of energy certification and sustainable design into pro forma modeling, pressure-testing the economics of suburban product at higher construction costs; regional Green Building codes are shifting capital allocation toward already-established builders with Passive House expertise like Wood Partners.

stories.title: Gwinnett County Rental Asset Trades for $67.2M
stories.excerpt: A 352-unit multifamily development in the Gwinnett County town of Lawrenceville has sold for $67.2 million. The Atlanta Business Chronicle reports that Oxford Properties was the seller and Sherman Residential was the buyer. The rental community is on land on the site of the former Northwoods County Club golf course. Lawrenceville is 30 miles NE of Atlanta. Developed by Oxford Properties in 2023, Celadon on Club features units with one-, two- and three-bedroom layouts. Community amenities include a 3,000-square-foot resort-style pool, a golf simulator and 16 acres of dedicated green space. Sherman Residential also owns two other apartment communities in the Atlanta metro area, as well as additional multifamily assets in North Carolina, Tennessee, Missouri, Arizona and Texas. The post Gwinnett County Rental Asset Trades for $67.2M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sherman Residential acquires Celadon on Club (352 units, Lawrenceville, GA) for $67.2M, $191K/unit.
Former golf-course site, developed 2023 by Oxford Properties; Sherman owns 5 other multifamily assets across Southeast.
Lawrenceville 30mi NE Atlanta; low per-unit basis suggests value-add or secondhand acquisition discounting.
stories.summary: Sherman Residential purchased Celadon on Club, a 352-unit multifamily community in Lawrenceville, Georgia (30 miles northeast of Atlanta), from Oxford Properties for $67.2 million ($191K per unit). The property, developed in 2023 on a former golf-course site, features one-, two-, and three-bedroom units and includes a resort-style pool, golf simulator, and 16 acres of green space. Sherman Residential operates five other multifamily assets across the Southeast.
stories.impact: Sub-$200K/unit pricing on a 2023-delivered asset in Atlanta submarket signals either market softness, value-add positioning, or portfolio rationalization by seller. For developers: Gwinnett County absorption and rental rate trends may be softer than comps; this is a cautionary signal to reprice recent Atlanta suburban stabilized yield assumptions downward and stress-test basis for new Atlanta-area ground-up projects.

stories.title: Morgan Stanley Fund Pays $93.1M for Florida Senior Housing Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Morgan Stanley Investment Management, through investment funds managed by Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing (MSREI), acquired a Class A seniors housing portfolio located in the Orlando and Tampa metropolitan areas. The portfolio includes two communities comprising 300 independent living, assisted living and memory care units serving residents in Central Florida. The portfolio comprises the 193-unit Sonata Lake Mary in Lake Mary, Fla., and the 106-unit The Preserve at Dunedin in Clearwater, Fla. Commercial Search reports that AgeWell sold the Lake Mary property for $60 million, while Berkshire Residential Investments sold the Clearwater community for $31.1 million. AgeWell will continue to operate the communities. Funds managed by MSREI have been actively investing in seniors housing since 2022 and today maintain ownership interests in 13 senior living communities across the United States. The post Morgan Stanley Fund Pays $93.1M for Florida Senior Housing Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Morgan Stanley Investment Management acquires 300-unit seniors housing portfolio (Orlando, Tampa) for $93.1M.
Two properties: Sonata Lake Mary (193 units, Lake Mary, $60M) and Preserve at Dunedin (106 units, Clearwater, $31.1M).
MSREI maintains 13 senior living communities nationally; AgeWell remains operator; stabilized, income-producing assets.
stories.summary: Morgan Stanley Investment Management, through MSREI, acquired a two-property seniors housing portfolio in Central Florida for $93.1 million. The portfolio includes the 193-unit Sonata in Lake Mary (purchased for $60M) and the 106-unit Preserve at Dunedin in Clearwater (purchased for $31.1M). AgeWell will continue operating both communities. MSREI now owns 13 senior living communities across the U.S. following active investment since 2022.
stories.impact: Institutional capital demonstrating confidence in Florida seniors housing fundamentals amid demographic tailwinds (aging Boomer population, in-migration). For multifamily developers: Seniors housing asset pricing and cap rates in Florida are stabilizing institutional investor appetite; does NOT directly affect market-rate multifamily supply or demand, but signals that capital competing for Florida real estate is diversifying into specialized housing, potentially reducing capital availability for traditional apartment development.

stories.title: Joint Venture Lands $44M Refi for Tampa-Area Apartments
stories.excerpt: Mast Capital and Rockpoint obtained $44 million in refinancing for The Harlow, a 248-unit, Class A, garden-style multifamily community in Wesley Chapel, Florida. Berkadia’s Mitch Sinberg, Scott Wadler, Matthew Robbins, Brad Williamson, and Bryan Brown of Berkadia’s Miami and Boca Raton offices arranged the financing on behalf of the joint venture. Walton Street Capital provided the three-year, floating-rate loan, which refinances the property’s existing construction loan and provides the sponsors with the flexibility to pursue a sale or permanent financing over the coming years. The property was 98% occupied at closing. Completed in 2024, The Harlow is a four-story, Class A multifamily community situated on approximately 16.24 acres at 5101 Bruce B Downs Blvd. The 248-unit property offers a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom residences averaging approximately 1,006 square feet, complemented by a comprehensive amenity program that includes a pool and sundeck, a fitness studio, a walking trail, EV charging stations, and detached garages, and a clubhouse with co-working spaces and private offices. The post Joint Venture Lands $44M Refi for Tampa-Area Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Mast Capital and Rockpoint refinance The Harlow (248 units, Wesley Chapel, FL) for $44M, floating-rate, 3-year term.
Walton Street Capital provided loan; property 98% occupied at closing; Completed 2024; Class A garden-style.
Sponsors gain flexibility for future sale or permanent financing; EV charging, detached garages, co-working amenities.
stories.summary: A Mast Capital and Rockpoint joint venture secured $44 million in refinancing for The Harlow, a 248-unit Class A garden-style community in Wesley Chapel, Florida. Walton Street Capital provided a three-year, floating-rate loan that refinances the property's existing construction loan. The 2024-completed property was 98% occupied at closing and includes amenities such as EV charging, detached garages, fitness studio, and co-working spaces.
stories.impact: Strong 98% occupancy and successful refi into permanent debt for newly-completed Tampa-area product signals healthy absorption and unit economics; floating-rate structure reflects sponsor confidence in rate stability or intent to exit within 3 years. For developers: Wesley Chapel and West Tampa submarkets are demonstrating Class A absorption strength sufficient to support institutional refinancing; underwriting new Tampa-area development should assume strong lease-up and pricing consistent with achieved rents at The Harlow.

stories.title: Amid Higher-for-Longer Mortgage Rates, Multifamily Pros Find a Silver Lining
stories.excerpt: Nearly four years after mortgage rates surpassed 6 percent for the first time since the height of the 2008 financial crisis, borrowing conditions for homeowners and prospective buyers have remained stubbornly elevated with no signs of abating anytime soon. The average U.S. 30-year fixed mortgage rate went up to 6.02 percent from 5.89 percent for the week ending Sept. 15, 2022, marking the first time since November 2008 it had crossed that 6 percent threshold. Mortgage rates eventually spiked to near 8 percent in late 2023 and only briefly came down just below 6 percent for the week ending Feb. 26, 2026, before soaring once again once the war with Iran started in late winter. The latest Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey reported a weekly average for 30-year loans of 6.66 percent for the week ending Aug. 27, up from 6.56 percent in the year-ago period and in stark contrast to the 2.67 percent rate seen in December 2020. The reality of higher-for-longer mortgage rates persisting for the foreseeable future has quickly settled in for commercial real estate players, creating another variable to contend with along with inter-related elevated interest and capitalization rates. While the higher home-borrowing costs have created downward pressure for some condominium developers, the multifamily and adjacent single-family rental sectors have been a beneficiary, with more renters and fewer buyers in the market now. “The outlook for multifamily remains bright, largely due to rising rental demand from households priced out of homeownership,” said Chad Tredway, global head of real estate at J.P. Morgan Asset Management. “Buying a home is approximately 50 percent more expensive than renting a house. bullets: 30-year mortgage rates at 6.66% (Aug 2026), up from 6.56% YoY; peaked near 8% in late 2023.
Rates have remained elevated since surpassing 6% in Sept 2022; 'higher-for-longer' regime now entrenched.
Mortgage cost burden pushes renters into multifamily; commercial borrowers face persistent construction and permanent financing headwinds.
stories.summary: The 30-year mortgage rate averaged 6.66% for the week ending August 27, 2026, up from 6.56% a year prior and far above the 2.67% rate in December 2020. Rates surpassed 6% for the first time since 2008 in September 2022, briefly dipped below 6% in February 2026, then spiked again after late-winter geopolitical tension. The 'higher-for-longer' environment is now accepted as persistent, reshaping CRE financing assumptions.
stories.impact: Sustained high mortgage rates force more renters to remain in multifamily longer, supporting demand fundamentals and rent growth. However, elevated SOFR/floating-rate debt makes construction financing and bridge loans expensive; developers face pressure to lock permanent or low-leverage financing early or accept higher equity return requirements. This favors capital-strong, yield-focused operators over speculative builders; development starts in secondary markets face headwinds unless rents have already risen to offset higher carrying costs.

stories.title: Reuben Brothers’ Jordana Yechiel On the Firm’s Big Bet on Century City
stories.excerpt: Century City has long been one of Los Angeles’ most concentrated office districts, but Reuben Brothers is betting that the area’s next chapter will look far more residential, experiential and luxury-driven. At Century Plaza, the development firm is building up around the Fairmont Century Plaza hotel and Park Elm condominiums, layering in restaurants, galleries, expansive wellness offerings and a revamped public plaza. For Jordana Yechiel (nee Reuben) of Reuben Brothers, the strategy reflects a larger shift in how people want to live in Los Angeles, drawing inspiration from Dubai’s International Financial Centre becoming a round-the-clock destination, where restaurants, culture and residences transformed what had largely been a business district. Commercial Observer spoke with Yechiel in late August about why Reuben Brothers made such a large bet on Century City, what luxury buyers expect, and how the firm is curating tenants rather than chasing occupancy and rent. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: Reuben Brothers has traditionally focused on trophy real estate and hospitality. What made Century City and this project fit the portfolio? Jordana Yechiel: At Reuben Brothers, the anomaly in our portfolio is Century City. We started as a traditional real estate company, and then we went into hospitality and luxury hotels and some residential development. But these were always trophy assets, whether they were in London, or the Surrey Hotel on the Upper East Side, or we’ve now made the Waldorf Astoria out of the W in South Beach. Real trophy property first, hospitality second. So we look at the property as a property deal, because that’s the way our brains are wired, and then we bring the luxury to it. This is a new development. We’ve poured more money into this than anything else. Our belief behind this was we don’t want to just put more stuff out into the world. We want to say, “What’s missing? What’s working? How can we help?
bullets: Reuben Brothers transforming Century City office district into mixed-use luxury hub around Fairmont Century Plaza.
Park Elm Residences (luxury condos), new restaurants, galleries, wellness, revamped public plaza; model inspired by Dubai IFC.
Strategy reflects shift in LA luxury demand toward experiential, 24/7 residential-driven mixed-use over traditional office.
stories.summary: Reuben Brothers is executing a major redevelopment of Century City around the Fairmont Century Plaza hotel, adding luxury residential (Park Elm Residences condominiums), restaurants, galleries, expansive wellness offerings, and a revamped public plaza. The strategy mirrors Dubai's International Financial Centre model, transforming an office-centric district into a round-the-clock, residential-driven destination with curated tenants prioritizing experience over traditional occupancy targets.
stories.impact: Century City office-to-mixed-use conversion signals that LA luxury market demands experiential, walkable, mixed-use product over standalone office or residential; this validates the premium pricing and entitlement effort required for large-scale, curated mixed-use development in LA. For developers: trophy mixed-use projects are capturing institutional and luxury buyer/renter demand; pure-play office development in traditional office parks faces displacement risk unless repositioned as mixed-use anchors with residential and hospitality components.

stories.title: Downtown D.C. Office Conversion Secures $176M Loan, New Majority Partner
stories.excerpt: One of Washington, D.C.’s largest office-to-residential redevelopments has secured a new majority partner and $175.6 million in construction financing. A partnership of Stonebridge, the Bernstein Companies and Criterion Real Estate Capital sold a 72 percent stake in the conversion of 1990 K Street NW to an entity managed by MetLife Investment Management for $58.7 million, according to records reported by the Business Journals. Kennedy Wilson Capital led the financing along with U.S. Fire Insurance, North River Insurance, Odyssey Reinsurance and Allied World Assurance. Cushman & Wakefield’s D.C.-based capital markets and debt advisory team arranged the financing. The roughly $250 million redevelopment, which will be rebranded as 1999 Eye Street NW, will replace the former office building with a 14-story, 412,000-square-foot mixed-use property. Plans call for 340 market-rate apartments, 44 affordable units, 50 student housing units totaling 200 beds, along with 15,600 square feet of retail and 189 parking spaces. Bernstein bought the property for $55.8 million in 2001, and Stonebridge and Criterion joined the ownership group last year. The conversion is part of Mayor Muriel Bowser Housing in Downtown program, which provides a 20-year tax abatement for office-to-residential conversions or redevelopments. Demolition started in September 2025. The project is part of D.C.’s Housing in Downtown program, which offers a 20-year tax abatement for qualifying commercial-to-residential conversions and redevelopments. It is the second-largest project in the program’s pipeline, behind the planned conversion of the Universal Buildings on Connecticut Avenue into roughly 600 units. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Downtown DC office-to-residential conversion (1990 K Street) secures $175.6M construction financing and MetLife as 72% majority partner.
412K SF, 14-story mixed-use: 340 market-rate units, 44 affordable, 50 student housing, 23K SF retail/office.
Part of DC Mayor Bowser's Housing in Downtown initiative; lenders: Kennedy Wilson, USFire, North River, Odyssey Reinsurance.
stories.summary: A major Washington, D.C. office-to-residential conversion at 1990 K Street NW (to be rebranded 1999 Eye Street NW) secured $175.6 million in construction financing and a new majority partner: MetLife Investment Management acquired a 72% stake for $58.7 million. The $250 million redevelopment will deliver 412,000 SF across 14 stories, including 340 market-rate apartments, 44 affordable units, 50 student housing units, and 23K SF of retail and office space. Kennedy Wilson Capital and insurance partners led the financing.
stories.impact: Institutional capital (MetLife) and syndicated insurance-backed debt validating downtown DC office conversion economics signals strong pre-leasing, pricing, and local demand fundamentals. For developers: DC's Housing in Downtown program is creating a favorable entitlement/incentive environment for large-scale conversions; this compresses the timeline and risk for projects targeting DC's undersupplied downtown core, making conversion-based development more competitive versus greenfield suburban projects on a risk-adjusted basis.
